set.def: feeling very happy and full of energy, often because something good is about to happen

why: 'because something good is about to happen' was too narrow; people are also excited about things happening now

cloze.s: When Yuki first heard “it’s raining cats and dogs,” she thought animals were ___ falling from the sky.

why: old cloze showed the emphatic slang use and 'honestly'/'seriously' also fit it; new cloze shows the literal sense; 'really' dropped from syn as it pushes the intensifier sense
near-synonyms of 'actually/really'; would be defensible answers for the synonym question
hardly/fairly are near-opposites for the opposite question (ant slightly/mildly); definitely and fairly also fill the cloze
'you need to register online before Friday' fits the cloze sensibly
'Would you purchase the window seat or the aisle seat' fits the cloze
'ready' as a verb is not recognizable to learners; 'arrange' is not a synonym of prepare

set.def: an official agreement, usually written, between people or companies that the law can make them keep

why: contracts can be spoken; 'written' alone was inaccurate
near-opposite of opposition (ant: support, approval); would be a defensible answer to the opposite question
'pay an exact amount of twenty dollars' fits the cloze
'sold well, specifically/obviously because a famous actor praised it' both fit the cloze
def 'by many people or in many places' is a near-synonym of everywhere
'Every child will deserve a small gift' fits the cloze sensibly
'cope' means deal with a difficulty, not succeed in doing something; not a synonym in this sense

ex: Lightning can strike the same place more than once.
A falling branch struck Hannah’s car and cracked the windshield.

why: 'smash' means break violently, not a synonym; 'strike the ball into the outfield' is unnatural and confusing since a 'strike' in baseball means a miss
'the fans stayed on their feet constantly' fits the cloze
'strange' is a forced opposite of usual
near-opposite of random (ant planned/deliberate); defensible answer to the opposite question
near-opposite of protect (ant endanger/harm); defensible answer to the opposite question
'the living room was a variety of cups, plates, and wrapping paper' fits the cloze
'the dessert was truly good' fits the cloze
'I definitely believe that you did your best' fits the cloze
'Wear a helmet for insurance' is a sensible figurative fill of the cloze
'height' is a forced opposite of depth
'rival' means a competitor, not someone who hates or fights you
'The nurse properly watched the patient's heart rate' fits the cloze
'suit' means to look good on someone, not to be the right size; not a synonym in this sense

ex: The plan to close the park met strong resistance from neighbors.
When the company tried to cut lunch breaks, it ran into resistance from almost every worker.

why: 'body's resistance to illness' shows a different sense (ability to fight off disease) than the def

ex: My grandfather has conservative tastes and always wears a plain suit and tie.
The small town is conservative, and many people there were unhappy when the old church was turned into a bar.

why: 'conservative estimate' shows the cautious/low-guess sense, not the def's 'keep traditional ways' sense
'reply' is a spoken or written answer; a reaction can be a feeling or action, so not a synonym
